request.description:
**Surface:** WEB  
**View:** `WebWebinarMainPageViewV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `web-events-webinar-main-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** AllowAny

`GET web-api/v1/events/webinar-main-page/?login_type=pre_login|post_login`

The webinar landing feed, in five buckets, for both sides of login.

RUDIMENTARY FIRST PASS, by request. It reads what the schema already supports and adds no new columns, no cache and no pagination. What it does get right is the shape, because that is the part a client codes against and the expensive thing to change later.

ONE ENDPOINT FOR BOTH LOGIN STATES, NOT TWO. The two surfaces answer the same question and share four fifths of their query plan; splitting them would duplicate the visibility rules, which is precisely where two surfaces drift apart. The parameter selects the surface, and it is also what decides which `WebinarPriority` rows apply - that table is keyed per login state for the same reason.

AUTHENTICATION IS OPTIONAL AT THE FRAMEWORK LAYER AND MANDATORY AT THE APPLICATION LAYER, which is the only arrangement that works here. DRF resolves `permission_classes` during dispatch, BEFORE the view can read `login_type` - so `IsAuthenticated` would 401 the anonymous pre-login caller this endpoint exists to serve, and there is no permission class that can branch on a query parameter it has not been handed. `AllowAny` plus an explicit check inside `get()` is therefore the design, not a relaxation:

- `pre_login`  - served anonymously. A bearer token, if one is sent, is still resolved and still ignored; the caller asked for the signed-out page and gets it.
- `post_login` - refused with 401 unless the request authenticated.

`JWTAuthentication` is still installed, and that matters: it returns `None` when there is no `Authorization` header (so the request is anonymous and pre-login works), and RAISES `AuthenticationFailed` for a header that is present but bad. A malformed or expired token is therefore REJECTED on both branches - including `pre_login` - rather than silently downgraded to the anonymous page, which is the correct answer: a client sending a broken token has a problem it needs to see.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THAT REJECTION ARRIVES AS 401, with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`, because `MilesPlatform.authentication.JWTAuthentication` now implements `authenticate_header()` (measured). The 401 this view returns itself is a DIFFERENT case with the same status: a well-formed anonymous request asking for the post-login page, which the authenticator never rejects.

THE FIVE BUCKETS, and which of them the anonymous surface can populate:

`highlight_webinars`  Editorial. Driven by `WebinarPriority` rows for

```
THIS login state, lowest `priority` first. The
absence of a row is the signal - a webinar with no
active row for this state is not ranked last, it
is simply not here. Available pre-login.
```

`upcoming_webinars`   Everything visible in this state that has not

```
started, soonest first. Available pre-login.
```

`completed_webinar`   Per-user. Past webinars the user ATTENDED, each

```
tagged `eligible`. Post-login only.
```

`absent_webinar`      Per-user. Past webinars the user booked and did

```
not attend. Post-login only.
```

`missed_webinar`      Past webinars the caller is not committed to.

```
AVAILABLE PRE-LOGIN (2026-09-18): signed in it is
"never booked, or booked and then CANCELLED by
either side"; anonymously the caller has no
bookings, so it is every past webinar in the
window - which is what they have missed by not
being signed up.
```

SO PRE-LOGIN POPULATES THREE OF THE FIVE - `highlight_webinars`, `upcoming_webinars` and `missed_webinar`. The two that stay empty are the two that are statements about a BOOKING, which an anonymous caller does not have. Post-login populates all five, the three past ones from the caller's own attendance.

EVERY KEY IS ALWAYS PRESENT, EMPTY RATHER THAN OMITTED. A client that has to test for a key's existence before reading it will eventually forget to, and an absent key and an empty list mean the same thing to a rendering loop but different things to a null check. Fixed shape, varying contents.

WHAT `eligible` MEANS, AND THAT IT IS A DECISION. It is true when the booking's `attended_status` is `"1"` (attended), or when leadership force-overrode it on `BookingDetails`.

REWRITTEN 2026-09-15. This paragraph used to describe eligibility as an OR over two per-product booleans, `attended_status_caira` and `attended_status_non_caira`, "kept separate on that model so a CAIRA and a non-CAIRA webinar can be judged by different rules". Both columns were REMOVED on 2026-09-15: nothing in the tree ever wrote either of them, so the OR was false for every attended learner and eligibility came out false unless leadership intervened. Product is now carried by the `subject` FK on `Webinar`, and attendance by the single `attended_status` code.

It still deliberately does NOT recompute eligibility from `attended_webinar_duration_seconds` against `total_webinar_duration_seconds` - all three are now the same unit, seconds, but the point stands: the thresholds live in the attendance ingest, and a second implementation of a rule that already exists elsewhere is a rule that will disagree with itself.

KNOWN LIMITS OF THIS PASS, none of them silent:

- NO ENROLMENT FILTERING. `show_webinar_as_per_enrollment` (CPA / CMA / CAIRA / USP) is NOT applied, so the post-login upcoming list is wider than a finished implementation's would be. Applying it needs the caller's enrolment set, which is an `Accounts` read this pass does not make.
- NO CACHE. Every call hits Postgres. The two anonymous buckets are identical for every visitor and are the obvious first thing to cache.
- NO PAGINATION - a hard cap instead, see `_MAIN_PAGE_MAX_ROWS`.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `login_type` - Required. One of: `pre_login`, `post_login`. One of pre_login / post_login.

---

> From `EVENTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



## 6. `GET web-api/v1/events/webinar-main-page/`

The webinar landing feed, in five buckets, for both sides of login. Web only.

This is a rudimentary first pass by request. The shape is the part that is settled; the bucket rules are
deliberately simple and each is a single filter, so a product correction is a one-line change.

### 6.1 Query parameters

| Param | Type | Required | Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `login_type` | string | yes | `pre_login`, `post_login` |

DELIBERATELY REQUIRED, WITH NO DEFAULT. Defaulting to `pre_login` would mean a signed-in client that forgot the
parameter silently receives the anonymous page - a valid 200 that is wrong, with the two booking buckets empty
rather than absent. Omitting it is a 400 naming the parameter.

The vocabulary is `pre_login` / `post_login`, with underscores. Those two literals are the stored values in the
database columns this endpoint filters on, so there is one vocabulary end to end and no translation map.

### 6.2 Authentication is conditional

| `login_type` | Anonymous request | Request with a valid token | Request with a BAD token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pre_login` | `200` | `200`, token resolved and ignored | `403` |
| `post_login` | `401 authentication_required` | `200` | `403` |

This is the only route in the app that is reachable anonymously and also serves per-user data. The branch
cannot live in a permission class - DRF resolves permissions during dispatch, before any view has read a query
parameter - so the view carries `AllowAny` and enforces the rule itself. It is a design, not a missing
`IsAuthenticated`.

A malformed or expired token is rejected on BOTH branches, including `pre_login`, rather than silently
downgraded to the anonymous page: a client sending a broken token has a problem it needs to see. That rejection
is the `403` from 1.2. The `401` here is the different case - a well-formed anonymous request asking for the
signed-in page - and it carries `message`, not `detail`:

```json
{
  "status": "error",
  "code": "authentication_required",
  "message": "login_type=post_login requires an authenticated request. Send a bearer token, or ask for login_type=pre_login."
}
```

### 6.3 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Webinar main page retrieved successfully.",
  "data": {
    "login_type": "post_login",
    "highlight_webinars": [],
    "upcoming_webinars": [],
    "completed_webinar": [],
    "absent_webinar": [],
    "missed_webinar": []
  }
}
```

EVERY KEY IS ALWAYS PRESENT, EMPTY RATHER THAN OMITTED. Fixed shape, varying contents - a rendering loop treats
an absent key and an empty list the same way, but a null check does not.

`pre_login` POPULATES THREE OF THE FIVE (amended 2026-09-18): `highlight_webinars`, `upcoming_webinars` and
`missed_webinar`. The two that stay empty are `completed_webinar` and `absent_webinar`, which are statements
about a BOOKING that an anonymous caller does not have. `post_login` populates all five, the three
backward-looking ones from the caller's own attendance.

The two plural keys and the three singular keys are inconsistent, and that is preserved deliberately: they
match the requested contract, and renaming a client contract to tidy it is a breaking change for cosmetic gain.

### 6.4 The five buckets

| Bucket | Per-user? | What is in it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `highlight_webinars` | no | Editorial. Driven by priority rows for THIS login state, lowest priority first. The absence of a row is the signal - an unranked webinar is not last, it is simply not here. Upcoming only. |
| `upcoming_webinars` | no | Everything visible in this login state that has not started, soonest first. |
| `completed_webinar` | yes | Past webinars the user ATTENDED. Each carries `eligible`. Post-login only. |
| `absent_webinar` | yes | Past webinars the user booked and did not attend. Post-login only. |
| `missed_webinar` | partly | Past webinars the caller is not committed to. BOTH login states - see below. |

`highlight_webinars` is a curated rail over the same webinars as `upcoming_webinars`, so the two lists overlap
by design. De-duplicate on `id` if your layout needs to.

Every bucket is capped at 20 rows. There is no pagination - this is a landing page, not a catalogue. The three
backward-looking buckets look back 90 days.

`absent` and `missed` are disjoint and the split is a product decision, not a schema fact: ABSENT is a live
booking the user did not honour, MISSED is a webinar they are not committed to.

THE ROUTING IS BY `attended_status`, AMENDED 2026-09-18. A booking the user CANCELLED now lands in
`missed_webinar`; it previously appeared in no bucket at all, so a cancelled webinar vanished from the page.

| `attended_status` | Bucket |
| --- | --- |
| `1` attended | `completed_webinar` |
| `2` not attended | `absent_webinar` |
| `3` registered | `absent_webinar` |
| `""` MF has not reported yet | `absent_webinar` |
| `4` cancelled | `missed_webinar` |
| no booking row at all | `missed_webinar` |

Cancellation reaches this endpoint on two independent columns - `status = false` (this system cancelled the
booking) and `attended_status = "4"` (MF reported it cancelled) - and BOTH route to `missed_webinar`, so the
same user action does not land in different buckets depending on which side recorded it.

ATTENDANCE OUTRANKS CANCELLATION. `attended_status = "1"` is `completed_webinar` even on a cancelled booking:
attendance is a fact about a session that already happened, a cancellation is a statement of intent about it,
and `completed_webinar` is the only bucket carrying `eligible` - so routing an attended row elsewhere would
withdraw the CPE / badge affordance from someone who earned it.

---

## 8. The webinar card, shared by all five main-page buckets

All five buckets carry identical objects, so one view model reads `highlight_webinars[0]` and
`missed_webinar[0]` alike.

```json
{
  "id": "3f1a9c7e-5b42-4d9a-8f10-2c6be7d41a55",
  "slug": "caira-level-1-orientation",
  "name": "CAIRA Level 1",
  "type": "webinar",
  "short_description": "...",
  "start_date_time": "2026-09-20T13:00:00+00:00",
  "end_date_time": "2026-09-20T14:00:00+00:00",
  "duration_seconds": 3600,
  "webinar_zoom_id": "84123456789",
  "is_test_webinar": false,
  "webinar_why_attend_points": [],
  "webinar_what_will_you_learn_points": [],
  "subject": "CAIRA",
  "subject_details": {
    "id": "b2c4e1a8-7f39-4c52-9d61-08ab3e7f4d12",
    "subject": "CAIRA"
  },
  "level_details": {
    "level_id": "d57e0b93-1a46-4f88-ae20-6c91f2b7e034",
    "level_number": 1,
    "level_name": "Level 1",
    "level_actual_name": "Foundations of AI for Accountants"
  },
  "horizontal_thumbnail": "https://.../h.png",
  "vertical_thumbnail": "https://.../v.png",
  "square_image": "https://.../s.png",
  "fields_of_study": [{ "id": "...", "name": "Information Technology", "cpe_credit": 1.0 }],
  "total_cpe_credits": 1.0
}
```

| Key | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | UUID string | This is what you send to `register-via-zoom`. |
| `slug` | string or null | |
| `name` | string | |
| `type` | string | `webinar`, `offline`, `orientation`, `premier`. Only the first two are registrable here. |
| `short_description` | string | |
| `start_date_time` | ISO-8601 or null | |
| `end_date_time` | ISO-8601 or null | |
| `duration_seconds` | integer or null | **SECONDS** from 2026-09-25; one hour is `3600`. Was `duration_minutes`. |
| `webinar_zoom_id` | string or null | The id Zoom keys the session on. Distinct from the MF/SF ingest anchor. |
| `is_test_webinar` | boolean | Visible only to an internal test user, in either login state. An ordinary user never receives one. |
| `webinar_why_attend_points` | array of strings, or null | Editorial copy. `null` when the operator never authored any - not an empty array. |
| `webinar_what_will_you_learn_points` | array of strings, or null | Same. |
| `subject` | string or null | THE CAIRA / CAIBA ANSWER. See below. `null` when the webinar carries no level. |
| `subject_details` | object or null | `{id, subject}`. Null together with `subject`. |
| `level_details` | object or null | `{level_id, level_number, level_name, level_actual_name}`, or null. |

`subject` plus `level_details.level_number` is what renders "CAIRA L1". `level_details` is NULL AS A WHOLE
when the webinar has no level, so you test one key rather than four - and "no level" stays distinct from "a
level whose name happens to be blank", which four flat nulls cannot express. `subject_details` is null
together with `subject`, for the same reason.

**`subject_details` AND `level_details.level_id` WERE ADDED ON 2026-09-17.** Both are additive - nothing was
removed or renamed, and `subject` stays exactly where it was because shipped clients read it. They exist
because **a name is not an address**: `Subject.name` is not unique, and a level's generated `level_name`
("Level 1") repeats across every subject, so neither could be used to link anywhere. The subject name is
REPEATED inside `subject_details` on purpose - a client rendering from that object should not have to reach
back out to a sibling key for its label.
| `horizontal_thumbnail` | URL string, `""` when unset | |
| `vertical_thumbnail` | URL string, `""` when unset | |
| `square_image` | URL string, `""` when unset | |
| `fields_of_study` | array | `{id, name, cpe_credit}` per active field of study. Empty array when nothing is tagged. |
| `total_cpe_credits` | float or null | The SUM of the above. `null`, not `0`, when nothing is tagged. |

**`total_cpe_credits` WAS `cpe_credits` UNTIL 2026-09-18** - a rename, with no alias kept. It is the sum over
`fields_of_study`, each of which carries its own `cpe_credit` (singular), and the old plural read as the same
quantity as the per-entry one. The rename is scoped to this payload: `Masterclass` course payloads and the
Netcore activity params still send `cpe_credits`, deliberately.

`caira_check` and `non_caira_check` are DELIBERATELY NOT EMITTED on this endpoint (they are on `all-bookings`).
They are two booleans describing the same thing `subject` describes properly, and a client given both would
have to decide which wins. Use `subject`.

### 8.1 `registration` - on `highlight_webinars` and `upcoming_webinars`, `post_login` only

```json
"registration": {
  "status": "SUCCESS",
  "registration_status": "REGISTERED",
  "attempt_id": "9c2f...",
  "join_url": "https://us06web.zoom.us/w/8412...",
  "error_code": null,
  "error_message": null,
  "zoom_attempts": 1,
  "completed_at": "2026-09-17T09:14:22.118+00:00",
  "route_to_web_lms": false
}
```

Same three-state contract as section 3.2 - branch on `registration_status`, not on `status`.

The key is ABSENT on the `pre_login` branch (anonymous callers have no registration to report) and on the three
past buckets (registration is an affordance - register vs join - and a webinar that already happened offers
neither; `completed_webinar` answers the question those rows raise with `eligible` instead).

A user who registered before the attempt-row pipeline existed has a booking and no attempt. That case comes
back as `registration_status: "REGISTERED"` with `status`, `attempt_id`, `join_url` and `completed_at` all
`null` and `zoom_attempts: 0`. Do not read "no attempt id" as "not registered" - registering again would spend
another Zoom registrant slot on a seat they already hold.

`route_to_web_lms` is `true` only for an internal test user on a CAIRA webinar today. When `true`, open the
session in the web-LMS surface instead of `join_url`.

### 8.2 `eligible` - on `completed_webinar` only

Boolean. `true` when the booking's `attended_status` is `"1"` (attended), or when leadership force-overrode it.

It is deliberately NOT recomputed from `attended_webinar_duration_seconds` against `total_webinar_duration_seconds`: the
thresholds live in the attendance ingest, and a second implementation of a rule that already exists elsewhere
is a rule that will disagree with itself.

---

### 9.1 `one_on_one` is always empty today

Reading 1:1 bookings works. Nothing in this repository CREATES one yet - the career-counselling write path is
not ported. So the `one_on_one` list is empty until that lands or historical rows are migrated in. An empty
list is not a fault. Build the card anyway; the shape is final.

Of the four `booking_type` values, only `career` can be newly booked. `office`, `resume` and `alumni` remain
legal to READ so historical rows keep resolving, so a reader must accept all four.

### 9.2 `webinar-main-page` does not filter by enrolment

`show_webinar_as_per_enrollment` (CPA / CMA / CAIRA / USP) is NOT applied, so the `post_login` upcoming list is
wider than a finished implementation's would be. Applying it needs the caller's enrolment set, which this pass
does not read.

### 9.6 No caching, no pagination on `webinar-main-page`

Every call hits Postgres, and the buckets are hard-capped rather than paginated. Expect that to change behind
the same response shape.

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `BrochureDownloadViewV1`  
**Module:** `Accounts.views`  
**Route name:** `brochure-download-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces 3 legacy MilesOne routes:** `POST caira/hitting-net-enquiry-for-brochure/`, `POST cpa/hitting-net-enquiry-for-brochure/`, `POST cma/hitting-net-enquiry-for-brochure/`

`POST api/v1/brochure-download/?programme=CAIRA|CPA|CMA`

Records a brochure download: files a Salesforce lead, books the learner into that ONE programme's next webinar, and pushes the Netcore `brochure_downloaded` event.

ONE ROUTE FOR THREE BROCHURES AS OF 2026-09-29 (maintainer). It replaced `_FunnelLeadViewV1` and its three subclasses - `caira/`, `cpa/` and `cma/brochure-download/` - which were three paths, three classes and one body. All three 404 now, with no shim.

THE URLCONF ARGUED AGAINST EXACTLY THIS, AND THE ARGUMENT IS RECORDED THERE RATHER THAN DELETED. It held that a path segment is unspoofable and unomittable, so which brochure was tapped could not be lost. A REQUIRED `ChoiceField` on a `StrictInputSerializer` is the same guarantee by another mechanism - absent is a 400, unknown is a 400, and the vocabulary is closed. What the decision protected is intact; what it also bought, per-path permissioning and retirement, is what was given up, and these three never used it.

THE PROGRAMME IS A QUERY PARAMETER BECAUSE THERE IS NO BODY. These endpoints have never accepted one. Its sibling `api/v1/account/enquiry/` puts `programme` in the body, which looks inconsistent until you notice that endpoint already has a body for its optional `lead` block. Neither invents a container for one field.

A BODY IS STILL REFUSED, AND THAT IS CHECKED HERE. The query serializer never looks at one, so without this a caller could POST anything and be told it worked. Legacy got this for free from a field-less body serializer; the check moved rather than disappeared.

ONE AUDIENCE, NOT THE PATHWAY FAN-OUT, and no `course_id` on the lead - see `capture_brochure_download` for why those two are not the same decision.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `programme` - Required. One of: `CPA`, `CMA`, `CAIRA`. Which brochure was downloaded: CAIRA, CPA or CMA.

**No request body by design.** Programme is `?programme=`; no body is accepted.

---

> From `ACCOUNTS_API_CONTRACT_V1.md` - the contract the frontend web team works to.



### 10.2 The brochure route - the learner acted ON a programme

| Route | Audience booked | Netcore push |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST api/v1/brochure-download/?programme=CAIRA` | CAIRA | `brochure_downloaded` |
| `POST api/v1/brochure-download/?programme=CPA` | CPA | `brochure_downloaded` |
| `POST api/v1/brochure-download/?programme=CMA` | CMA | `brochure_downloaded` |

**ONE ROUTE, NOT THREE, SINCE 2026-09-30.** The three paths did the same work and differed only in
which programme their own URL named, which is a parameter wearing a path segment. `?programme=` is
required and validated against the three values above; anything else is a 400 rather than a 404, so a
typo says what was wrong with it.

**IT STILL TAKES NO BODY AT ALL.** Any key you send is a 400 - the serializer declares no fields, and
the programme arrives on the query string. The old `caira/`, `cpa/` and `cma/` paths answer 404 with no
shim.

**Exactly ONE audience is booked, not the pathway fan-out.** A CPA brochure tap names the programme;
routing it through the learner's pathway would also book them into CAIRA and CMA webinars off a signal
that said CPA. `enquiry/` with `programme: "CAIRA"` behaves the same way, for the same reason.

The lead itself is still filed against `user.pathway`, NOT against the brochure. The CRM's course field
answers "what are they buying" while the audience answers "what did they just look at", and legacy
filed it the same way.

### 10.3 What happens after the 200

The Salesforce lead is **awaited** - you are told whether it was recorded. The webinar booking and the
Netcore push are **detached**, and their outcome is not in the status code. A 200 means the lead was
filed; it does not mean a seat was confirmed.

Auto-registration fires even when Salesforce refused. A CRM outage is not a reason to withhold a
webinar seat from a learner who just expressed interest.

ONE BULK UPDATE, NOT A ROW-AT-A-TIME LOOP, so a learner with hundreds of notifications costs one statement. `count` in the response says how many rows actually changed, which is `0` on a second call - that makes it idempotent and safe to retry.

**View:** `CatalogueProductsViewV1`

**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

One page of active products, newest catalogue surface for both clients.

`GET api/v1/catalogue/products/?page=&page_size=&is_book=&search=`

UNIVERSAL. The app and the web ask the same question of the same catalogue and read the same answer, so this keeps the shared `api/` prefix rather than splitting by surface.

`ProductListQueryV1` validates the query STRICTLY, so an undeclared or misspelled parameter is a 400 rather than a silently ignored filter. `search` matches `title` case-insensitively as a substring; `is_book` is a tri-state - omit it for every product, send it to pick a side.

One of this learner's addresses - read it, edit it, or remove it.

`GET    api/v1/commerce/address/<address_id>/` `PATCH  api/v1/commerce/address/<address_id>/` `DELETE api/v1/commerce/address/<address_id>/`

UNIVERSAL. THE PATH CARRIES AN ID AND THE QUERYSET IS STILL USER-SCOPED. An object-id lookup that is not scoped to the caller is an IDOR, and this is the endpoint shape where that is easiest to forget.

SOMEONE ELSE'S ADDRESS IS A 404, NOT A 403, and the difference is the point: 403 would confirm the row exists and hand an attacker a membership oracle over the id space.

A DELETE THAT A SETTLED ORDER STILL POINTS AT IS A 409, NOT A DELETE. Every FK into an address is a historical record of where something was actually sent, and an order whose address vanished cannot be reconstructed. The learner is told to add a new address instead.

```
IsAuthenticated.

```
```
GET, PATCH, DELETE
```

```
200 OK: On read or edit.
204 No Content: On a successful delete.
404 Not Found: When the address is unknown or not this learner's.
409 Conflict: When an order references it.
400 Bad Request: On a malformed body.
```

THIS SURFACE STOPS SHORT OF PAYMENT. A cart can be built, priced and read, and nothing here turns it into an `Order` - the payment gateway is out of merge scope, and an endpoint that creates a paid order without a payment is worse than a missing one.

**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Add a variant to this learner's cart, or re-set its quantity.

`POST api/v1/commerce/cart/lines/`

UNIVERSAL. THE CART IS RESOLVED FROM THE TOKEN, never from the body, so a client cannot add a line to somebody else's cart.

ADDING THE SAME VARIANT TWICE SETS THE QUANTITY RATHER THAN RAISING. `com_uniq_checkout_variant` makes a duplicate line impossible, and a 409 for a double-tapped button is a worse answer than the obvious one. READ THE STATUS TO TELL THE TWO APART: `201` means a line was created, `200` means an existing line was updated. `created` carries the same fact in the body.

AN UNKNOWN OR RETIRED VARIANT IS A 404. H-14 makes retirement a soft flag, so a variant that is no longer sold answers the same as one that never existed - a caller holding a stale id learns the id is no good either way.

THE WHOLE REPRICED CART COMES BACK under `result`, not just the line that changed, so a client never has to follow a write with a read.

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
POST
```

```
200 OK: Updated.
404 Not Found: Unknown variant.
400 Bad Request: On a malformed body.
500 Internal Server Error: On an internal error.
```

**Methods on this view:** POST

Like or un-like one target as the calling learner.

Idempotent both ways: liking something already liked, or un-liking something never liked, is a 200 with `changed=False` and no counter movement. A double-tapped client needs no special case.

Scoped to `request.user` throughout - there is no way to like on another learner's behalf, which is why this is JWT-authenticated. That matters more here than on the private gestures: a like moves a PUBLIC counter, so a body-supplied user id would let any caller inflate a number everybody sees.

THE CLASS NAME IS UNCHANGED FROM THE `Likes` APP ON PURPOSE. It reads backwards - this is the endpoint that SETS a like, while "liked by me" sounds like a read - and renaming it is one of the five open maintainer decisions on record. It is not answered here just because the app around it moved.

**Module:** `Engagement.views`

**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Mark one target watched, or un-watch it.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: THE WRITER FOR `watched_by_me`, AND THREE SURFACES READ IT: the AI-in-Accounting reels feed (`watched_by_me` per card), Varun Masterclass (`is_watched` per clip) and the Programs stories rail (`watched` per story, `ProgramsPage/views.py::_watched_asset_ids`). All are `CMS.Asset` rows - the endpoint accepts `cms_asset` and nothing else. Before this endpoint's predecessor existed nothing wrote the row those feeds read, so the field was structurally incapable of being true. Ported from legacy's `POST /watched_by_me/` (`FileWatchedView`), which legacy shipped as a pair with the reels reader.

`Masterclass` IS DELIBERATELY NOT ONE OF THEM (maintainer, 2026-10-01). A course carries its own progress, chapter by chapter, in its own tables - a coarser "watched" here would be a second answer to a settled question, and it is not something a learner is shown. `_TARGETS['masterclass_course']` sets `interaction_fk = None` and the word is absent from `InteractionTargetKind`, so a watch naming a course is a 400 at the edge rather than a stored row.

THE THIRD READER NAMED HERE UNTIL 2026-10-01 WAS `IndustryUnplugged`, and that app is gone - its family left `_TARGETS` the same day, measured at zero rows in all three tables.

RENAMED FROM `ContentWatchedViewV1`, which lived in `HomepageContent`. The "Content" was accurate while homepage content was the only watchable thing; it stopped being accurate when `IndustryUnplugged` landed, and a class name that names one of the three families it serves is the kind of thing a reader trusts and should not.

Idempotent: sending the same value twice returns 200 with `changed=False`, so a client replaying a scroll event needs no special case. That path is also the CHEAPEST one - see `set_interaction`, which reads before it writes precisely because a player re-posts this on every playback.

              "long_description": "What brings down a company isn’t always bad business decisions or market crashes. Sometimes, it’s something far more silent. A missing approval. A bypassed review. A forged bank statement. Not a grand heist, but a slow and steady leak, dripping through the cracks of a broken system. And at the heart of that system? Weak or absent internal controls.

In this episode, Varun walks us through the most overlooked but most powerful safeguard in financial reporting: internal controls.

This isn’t just compliance talk. It’s the difference between order and chaos, between transparency and deception.

💼 Start with the Five Pillars of Internal Control:
1. Control Environment - A company’s ethical backbone. Without it, even the best policies collapse.
2. Risk Assessment - Spotting weaknesses before fraudsters do.
3. Information and Communication - Transparency wins. Secrecy gives fraud a place to hide.
4. Monitoring Activities - What isn’t reviewed isn’t controlled.  
5. Control Activities - The locks on the financial doors: segregation of duties, reconciliations, authorisations.

These are not optional features. They’re what turn a financial system into a fortress.

🚨 Then come the cautionary tales:
• Enron, once the darling of Wall Street, built on manipulated profits and hidden debt. When the truth came out, it wasn’t just the company that fell — it was investor confidence across the market.
• Satyam, often called India’s Enron, where the chairman personally inflated numbers with fake invoices and bank statements. Billions were wiped out overnight.
• Wells Fargo, where a culture of aggressive sales targets led to thousands of fake accounts. No one questioned the numbers until it was too late.
• Walmart, whose global ambitions stumbled over bribery scandals in Mexico, Brazil, China, and India — all because compliance took a back seat.

In each case, it wasn’t just a rogue employee or a one-off mistake. It was a failure of the system. Internal controls were ignored, bypassed, or overridden.

🎯 So, what does a strong internal control system really look like?
• Governance that starts at the top.
• Segregation of duties so no single person has too much control.
• Regular reviews and independent checks.
• And now, even AI and analytics to detect anomalies faster than humans ever could.

Fraud rarely happens in a flash. It builds in the silence of unchecked moments. But when internal controls are strong, they close the doors before anyone can sneak through.

A well-governed system doesn’t just protect a balance sheet, it protects reputation, investor trust, and long-term business integrity.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppAiInAccountingReelsViewV1`  
**Module:** `Homepage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-ai-in-accounting-reels-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The AI-in-Accounting reels feed for the app home screen.

GET /app-api/v1/home/ai-in-accounting-reels/?page=1&page_size=10

APP-ONLY, hence the `app-api/` prefix and the `App` marker on the class - the surface rule's reads-split-by-surface half. There is no web twin today.

PAGINATION IS `utils.pagination`, the module every paginated surface uses, so this feed answers with the same block as the Programs feed and the web lists. It slices in SQL and passes the true count; the module only builds the window and the block, so nothing here leaves the event loop. Defaults are the module's (6 per page, 100 ceiling), not legacy's 10 / 50.

A BAD `?page=` IS A 400 NOW, and so is any parameter this endpoint does not read. It used to fall back to page one, which hid a client building the query string wrong - the strict-input rule's case.

EVERY READ IS A `.values()` PROJECTION and the two per-caller flags are `Exists` subqueries, so nothing materialises a model instance and no lazily loaded relation is touched on the event loop.

Responses:

```
200 OK: `{"slug", "count", "page", "page_size", "total_pages",
"has_next", "has_previous", "next", "previous", "results": [...]}`.
THE LIST WAS `"ai_in_accounting"` UNTIL 2026-10-06, and
`"AI In Accounting"` before 2026-10-05 (legacy's spelling). It is
`results` now, as on every block `utils.pagination` builds. CLIENT
VISIBLE, and there is no alias.
400 Bad Request: a pagination value that is not a whole number, or a
query parameter this endpoint does not read.
200 OK with an empty list when the section is absent or deactivated -
NOT a 404. A section an editor turned off is a feed with nothing in it,
which is a normal state, not a missing resource.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppHomePageViewV1`  
**Module:** `Homepage.views`  
**Route name:** `app-home-page-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET homepage_V8_async/`

`GET app-api/v1/home/page/` - the whole app home page in one call.

Ported from legacy MilesOne's `/homepage_V8_async/`. THE `V8` WAS THEIRS, NOT OURS - this surface is v1 like everything else here, and the page's shape lives in the database rather than in a version number.

WHY ONE CALL. The app previously fanned out to the header, level, coming-soon, AI-Lab and referral endpoints separately, so the first screen cost five round trips on a phone network. This returns the lot.

THE PAGE IS DATA

```
Section order, titles and presence come from `CMS.Page` - a root row
with `page_slug="homepage"` and one active child per section, ordered
by `position`. What FILLS each section is decided by its slug, in
`_build_section`.
```

```
So re-ordering the page or renaming a heading is an admin edit. Only a
genuinely new KIND of section is a code change. Legacy hard-codes eleven
positions in the view, which is why every redesign there needed a whole
new endpoint.
```

EVERY ACTIVE SECTION SHIPS, EVEN EMPTY

```
`data` is always a list, and a section with nothing in it is `[]`
rather than omitted - so a rail that is merely empty today keeps its
slot and the client hides it.
```

```
WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A SECTION IS DEACTIVATED IS DIFFERENT, and this
paragraph used to get it wrong. A row with `active=False` is filtered
out by `_page_sections` and does NOT ship as an empty section.
```

```
THE GUARANTEE THAT ACTUALLY HOLDS is that the survivors keep their
numbers: `position` is STORED on each row, not computed from list order,
so deactivating Level 2 leaves Level 3 at position 7. It does not slide
up into 6 and start impersonating Level 2. That is the property worth
having, and it is the reason `position` is read from the database rather
than enumerated at render time - a computed ordinal would renumber
everything after any removal.
```

```
POSITIONS ARE 1..11 AND CONTIGUOUS, seeded by
`Miscellaneous/Scripts/load_home_page_sections.py`. They are a display
counter, not a sparse sort key.
```

TWO GATES, DELIBERATELY NOT THE SAME TEST

```
`is_enrolled`            hides the continue-watching rail.
`can_access_masterclass` decides whether there is a subscription to
                           sell, and rewrites a locked card's CTA.
```

```
A CPA-only learner is ENROLLED and still holds none of what the
subscription offers, so one test cannot do both jobs. The second runs
SERIALLY AFTER the enrolment refresh, because that refresh persists the
learner's programme list and the access category is derived from it -
running them concurrently would read the category off the previous value.
```

CACHING

```
Per learner, 30 seconds, keyed on the shared CMS content version - so an
admin edit to any page, section or card invalidates every cached copy
with one `INCR` rather than a sweep nothing can perform. The cache
holds the UNCAPPED payload; the per-section cap runs after it, on both
hit and miss, so changing the cap does not keep serving the old one for a
TTL.
```

NO QUERY PARAMS

```
Unknown ones are IGNORED, not rejected, so an old client still gets an
ordinary response. A section needing more than `SECTION_LIMIT` items
needs its own endpoint.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `AlumniBadgeClaimViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `alumni-badge-claim-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST caira/claim_alumni_badge/`

`POST api/v1/badges/alumni-claim/` - record that a learner claimed one.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `CAIRAClaimAlumniBadgeView` on 2026-09-29.

ON THE SHARED `api/` PREFIX, UNLIKE THE WALL ABOVE. Writes stay shared - a browser and a handset claiming a badge are doing the same thing, and splitting a write produces two routes that must never diverge. The READ split to `app-api/` because the card shape is the app's.

ONE UPDATE, NO SELECT. The ownership test is a filter clause rather than a fetch-then-compare, so a learner cannot claim somebody else's badge and the check costs nothing extra. `updated_count == 0` covers both "no such allocation" and "not yours", and they answer the same 404 deliberately - telling them apart tells an attacker which ids exist.

IDEMPOTENT. Claiming twice answers 200 both times; the column is already True on the second call and the update simply matches a row and writes the same value. A client retrying after a dropped response does not need to care.

IT DELETES THE WALL'S CACHE, which is the half legacy got wrong in a way worth naming: legacy deleted `CAIRA_ALUMNI_BADGES_USER_CACHE_PREFIX` while its own wall wrote and read `..._V2_USER_...`. One character of prefix apart, so the claim cleared a key nothing had written and the wall served `claimed_status: false` for the rest of its five-minute TTL - the button bounced back. Both sides here use the V2 prefix, and there is only one.

Body template generated from `AlumniBadgeClaimRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `LevelBadgeClickedViewV1`  
**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`  
**Route name:** `level-badge-clicked-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `POST caira/level_based_badge_clicked/`

`POST api/v1/badges/level-badge-clicked/` - claim a CAIRA level badge.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `CAIRALevelBasedBadgeClickedView` on 2026-09-29. Marks a CAIRA level badge as clicked and rewrites its stored accept URL from Credly's click-to-claim form (`.../badges/<assertion_id>/accept`) to the public assertion form (`.../badges/<assertion_id>`).

UNIVERSAL (maintainer, 2026-09-29), WHICH IS WHY IT TAKES TWO INPUT FORMS. It briefly shipped on `app-api/` because legacy's app and web handlers disagreed about the request body - the app sends the whole `credly_accept_url` it was handed, the web LMS has the bare id already - and two bodies cannot share a route. Accepting EITHER identifier removes that obstacle, so the write goes back where writes belong: one route, one column, no pair to keep in step. `LevelBadgeClickedRequestSerializerV1` holds the exactly-one-of rule.

THE CLIENT NEVER PARSES AN ASSERTION ID OUT OF A URL. Whichever form arrives, the extraction happens here, so the rule lives in one place instead of in every client that ever renders a badge.

BOTH URL FORMS ARE ACCEPTED - with and without the trailing `/accept` - so a client holding a pre-click URL from a stale cache still resolves. That is also what makes the endpoint idempotent: claiming twice sends the post-click form the second time, and it still finds the row.

`WebMasterclassLevelBasedBadgeClickedViewV1` STILL EXISTS AND STILL WRITES THE SAME COLUMN. It is the web LMS's own handler at `api/v1/masterclass-web/level-badge-clicked/`, and it answers a BOOLEAN `status` because every endpoint on that surface does. Retiring it is a web-client change, not a backend one, so it is left alone here - but it is now a second writer of `credly_badge_clicked_by_user` and should be retired once the web LMS can move to this envelope. Named here so the duplication is a decision on record rather than a surprise.

LEVEL BADGES ONLY. An assertion that resolves to a webinar, Masterclass course, alumni or archived allocation is a 400 naming the right endpoint, not a silent success - claiming an alumni badge here would leave the alumni wall's own `claimed_status` untouched.

Answers five things per programme: is the learner enrolled, are they alumni, have they claimed their alumni badge, are they logged into that programme's LMS, and what is their LMS token.

RECHECKED 2026-10-07: FIVE QUERIES, RUN ONE AFTER ANOTHER, none of them per programme - the enrolment tags, then four gathered in `programme_status_rows`. Django's async ORM runs each through `sync_to_async(thread_sensitive=True)` on one shared thread, so the `gather` does not overlap them. Only the live-template read spans the table; claims, LMS logins and flags are filtered to this learner. Adding a fifth programme costs no extra query.

Cached per learner for 30 seconds. USER-SCOPED KEY, necessarily - every field here is about one person, so a shared key would serve one learner's entitlements to another for the whole TTL.

"Other" named the endpoint by what it is NOT - it was the leftover beside the webinar badge views - which tells a reader nothing about what it returns; the subject is the ALUMNI badge, and the name now says so. And the route sat on the SHARED `api/` prefix while serving one surface: this is a read shaped for the app's alumni strip, so it splits by surface under the versioning standard, exactly as `AppBadgesPageViewV1` does. The claim itself is a write and stays on the shared prefix.

THE `-v1` MARKER IS CARRIED AS THE `V1` SUFFIX on the class, and by `app-alumni-badge-status-v1` on the route. The path has no `v1` segment of its own beyond the prefix, which is the same shape every `app-api/v1/` route uses.

Ported from legacy MilesOne `CAIRAGetAlumniBadgesView` (`caira/views.py`) on 2026-09-29.

THE THIRD BADGE ENDPOINT, AND THE THREE ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. Keep them straight before adding a field to the wrong one:

```
`badges/page/`           the CATALOGUE - every configured badge, with
                           the learner's state painted on top.
`badges/alumni-status/`  the FLAGS - five booleans per programme,
                           including LMS login state. No artwork.
here                       the CARDS - what the learner actually holds,
                           with the Credly URLs needed to claim one.
```

THREE STATES PER PROGRAMME, which is the whole shape of the response:

```
not enrolled     no card at all, and a message saying why.
enrolled, not    a card with the static artwork and the heading, and
alumni yet       nulls where the allocation's own values would go.
alumni           the full card, from the allocation row.
```

THE STATIC IMAGE URLS ARE LEGACY'S, CARRIED VERBATIM. They are Credly's own CDN, not ours, and they are what the app has rendered since this endpoint shipped - so they are constants here rather than a lookup that could answer differently. A card for a learner who is not yet alumni has no allocation to read an image off, and an empty card is worse than a greyed-out one.

CACHED PER LEARNER FOR 5 MINUTES, on a user-scoped key. Every field is about one person, so a shared key would serve one learner's badges to another for the whole TTL. The claim endpoint below deletes this key, so a claim is visible on the next read rather than up to five minutes later.

**Module:** `BadgeCertificateCPE.views`

**Methods on this view:** GET

**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

**Replaces legacy MilesOne** `GET caira/badges_catalog/V2/`

`GET app-api/v1/badges/page/` - the app's CPE Tracker badge wall.

A `cpe_summary` progress strip followed by four sections, in screen order: `level_badges`, `webinar_badges`, `masterclass_badges` and `global_certifications`.

CATALOGUE-CENTRIC, NOT EARNED-CENTRIC, and that is the whole difference from `AppAlumniBadgeStatusV1` beside it. That endpoint lists what a learner already holds; this one lists EVERY configured Production badge and paints the learner's state on top, so a learner with zero badges still gets a full wall of cards rather than an empty screen.

READ-ONLY. Every action a card fires - claim, feedback, register - already has its own endpoint, and the `cta` block names which.

THE FOUR SECTIONS

```
`level_badges`          one per active level with a Production badge,
                          ordered by level number, category-gated.
`webinar_badges`        CAIRA webinar badges, next session ascending,
                          cards with nothing scheduled last.
`masterclass_badges`    course badges, most actionable first.
`global_certifications` NON-CAIRA webinar badges, with their session.
```

THE CAIRA SPLIT IS WHY THE FOURTH SECTION EXISTS, and the two halves use the SAME predicate so a webinar cannot land in both or neither: `webinar_badges` takes `is_caira` true, `global_certifications` takes it false. Without the split a non-CAIRA webinar carrying a badge would appear twice in one response.

CACHING. Only the global catalogue layer is cached, partitioned by the test-viewer flag - see `badge_catalog`. The per-learner overlay is always fresh, because every field in it is an entitlement a learner acts on immediately, and a badge that does not change when it is claimed reads as a broken button.

`{}` IS NOT `null`. `next_session` and `cta` use an empty object for "nothing here", which is truthy in JavaScript - clients must test `Object.keys(x).length`.

PORTED FROM LEGACY MILESONE `CAIRABadgesCatalogAsyncViewV2`, 2026-09-28. The response contract is carried across; the reads underneath were rewritten against re-normalised models, and `badge_catalog`'s docstring holds the table. THREE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCES, each recorded where it happens:

1. `global_certifications` IS BUILT HERE, NOT BORROWED FROM THE EVENTS PAGE. Legacy instantiates the events view and calls five of its private methods, which this repository bans (H-21, no inline `protected-access`) and which would couple two endpoints' internals. The session half is projected through `EventsPage.serializers_page.card` instead - the SHAPE is shared, the pipeline is not - so a client keeps one binding. 2. THE CPE CREDIT IS DERIVED. Legacy reads a stored credit column that does not exist here; `EventsPage.utils.webinar_maps.acpe_map` sums the webinar's active fields of study, which is the one place CPE is derived. 3. THE TEST-WEBINAR GATE IS NEW. Legacy has no such flag; here it is the outermost gate and the catalogue cache is partitioned by it.

- `limit` - Optional. Default `0`. Per-section cap. 0 means use the endpoint's own default.
- `section` - Optional. One of level / webinar / masterclass / global_certifications.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL

**Module:** `AILabs.views`

**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** HasValidAILabsAssessmentSecret

INBOUND - the labs service posts a result to us.

Auth:

```
`HasValidAILabsAssessmentSecret` - header `X-AI-Labs-Secret` must
equal `settings.AI_LABS_X_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. NO JWT: the caller
is the labs service acting on a learner's behalf, so identity comes from
the BODY. An unset secret refuses every call, which is the correct
posture for an environment never meant to receive results.
```

Latch semantics:

```
`completed=False` is recorded and NEVER clears an already-set flag; a
redelivery is idempotent. Both are the latch's own guarantees.
```

THE `source` IS PINNED BY THE ENDPOINT and is deliberately NOT a body field: a partner holding the webhook secret must not be able to write itself into the audit trail as an operator decision (`admin_override`).

Responses:

```
`200` ALWAYS when the payload was understood - including for a
redelivery and for a learner with no enrollment. The labs service is a
fire-and-forget sender, and a 4xx to a retry-less caller loses the result
permanently, so anything we can record we accept and report in
`outcome`.
`400` only for a body we cannot read at all. `401` on a missing, wrong or unprovisioned secret.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** WEBHOOK  
**View:** `ZoomWebhookReceiverV1`  
**Module:** `EventsPage.views`  
**Route name:** `events-webhook-zoom-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** AllowAny

Receive Zoom events and register a webinar for poll-report ingestion.

POST /api/v1/events/webhook/zoom/

UNIVERSAL AND UNAUTHENTICATED BY DESIGN. Zoom is not a surface and holds no JWT, so `authentication_classes` is empty and `AllowAny` applies - the request is authenticated by an HMAC over its RAW body, verified here.

TWO EVENTS ARE HANDLED AND EVERYTHING ELSE IS A FAST 200:

- `endpoint.url_validation` - the one-time challenge Zoom runs when the endpoint is registered. It is NOT signed, so it is answered BEFORE signature verification; answering it after would make the endpoint impossible to register. Because that branch signs caller-supplied text while nothing has authenticated yet, the token is validated first - see `_url_validation`.
- `webinar.ended` - the real trigger. Resolves the webinar, upserts the tracking row with the verbatim envelope on it, and stops.

A NON-200 MAKES ZOOM RETRY, which is why an unusable event is ignored with a 200 rather than refused: a malformed body, an unknown webinar or an event this backend does not care about will never become usable, so a retry schedule against it is pure noise. 401 is reserved for the one case that is genuinely someone else's problem to fix - a bad signature.

IT DOES NOT ENQUEUE ANYTHING. The row is registered and the fetch is left to the sweep, because Zoom's report lags the end of the webinar and a Celery countdown longer than the Redis visibility timeout is redelivered repeatedly. See `EventsPage/tasks.py`.

SYNCHRONOUS, unlike every other view in this file. It does two short queries and no external I/O, and `hmac.compare_digest` plus `request.body` are both synchronous - an async wrapper here would add a thread hop to save nothing.

request.description:
**Surface:** WEBHOOK  
**View:** `CRMWebinarWebhookV1`  
**Module:** `Notification.views`  
**Route name:** `notification-webhook-crm-get-webinar-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** HasValidMilesOneWebhookSecretV1

POST one CRM/Events-CMS webinar payload, stored VERBATIM.

THE ONE ENDPOINT IN THIS APP WITHOUT A STRICT INPUT SERIALIZER, and that is deliberate. The body is a third party's record, kept whole in a JSON column with no mapping into the live `Webinar` model - normalisation is a later phase. A strict serializer would have to enumerate the CMS's field set and would reject every field it adds, which for a landing table is the wrong failure. Only `document_id` is required.

DEDUP IS AN UPSERT ON `document_id`. A repeat push overwrites the stored payload and RESETS the row to `received`, dropping any prior webinar link and `processed_at` - because a re-pushed payload makes earlier normalisation stale.

DELIVERY MODEL, and it drives the response codes: the CMS is fire-and-forget. It logs a non-2xx and does NOT retry, so RECHECKED 2026-10-07: any 400 or 401 (a rejected secret is 401, not 403) returned here means that event is permanently lost on the CMS side. Respond 2xx quickly.

Payload conventions, not to be fought: every field is always present with `null` for unset; the big-integer fields arrive as STRINGS to preserve precision and must stay strings; media fields are a URL or `null`.

Auth:

```
`X-Webhook-Secret` matching `MILES_ONE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. No JWT.
```

Responses:

```
201: created. 200: upserted. Both carry
    `{status, message, id, document_id, created}`.
400: body is not a JSON object, or `document_id` is missing.
401: header missing or wrong, or the secret is not configured.
```

Body template generated from `(verbatim CMS payload)`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

Authorised by the `X-Webhook-Secret` header, NOT by the bearer token. Set `{{miles_one_webhook_secret}}` in the environment.

body.raw:

request.description:
**Surface:** WEBHOOK  
**View:** `ReferralMilesForceWebhookViewV1`  
**Module:** `Referral.views`  
**Route name:** `referral-milesforce-webhook-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** none  
**Permission:** HasValidMilesForceVendorTokenV1

MilesForce tells us a referral's verdict.

POST /api/v1/referral/webhook/milesforce/

ANONYMOUS TO DRF, AUTHENTICATED BY A SHARED SECRET. MilesForce holds no JWT, so the only credential is the `x-vendor-token` header compared against `settings.X_VENDOR_TOKEN` by `HasValidMilesForceVendorTokenV1`.

THREE THINGS ABOUT THAT COMPARISON, ALL LOAD-BEARING, and all now the shared `SharedSecretPermission`'s rather than this view's:

```
1. `secrets.compare_digest`, not `==`. A plain comparison returns
   early on the first differing byte, which leaks the secret's prefix to
   anyone who can time the response.
2. AN UNSET SETTING REFUSES EVERY CALLER, with 401. If `X_VENDOR_TOKEN`
   is blank nothing is compared - an unconfigured environment must not be
   an open door onto a table that decides who gets paid. It answered 503
   until 2026-10-07; 401 is legacy's pinned contract and does not invite
   MilesForce to retry against an environment that will never accept it.
3. NO FALLBACK TO THE SETTING WHEN THE HEADER IS ABSENT. Legacy once
   substituted `settings.X_VENDOR_TOKEN` for a missing header and then
   compared it against itself, so a request with no credential matched.
   That was fixed in legacy and the fix is carried, named, so nobody
   reintroduces the convenience.
```

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: NOT enveloped (`NullForBlankJSONRenderer`).
200 OK: `ok`, `referral_id`, `status`, `matched_on`,
`forced_transition`, `updated_fields`, `unparsed_fields`.
400: a body that fails `MilesForceWebhookRequestSerializerV1` (missing
`id` / `bonus_status`, a non-UUID `referrance_id`, or an
undeclared key), or `{"detail": ...}` for a `bonus_status` we do not
recognise.
401: `{"detail": "A valid x-vendor-token header is required."}` for a
missing, wrong or unprovisioned vendor token, with no
`WWW-Authenticate` header (measured).
404: `{"detail": ...}` when no referral matched either key.
500: `internal_error_response`'s body, detail in the span.
```

Body template generated from `MilesForceWebhookRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

Authorised by the `x-vendor-token` header, NOT by the bearer token. Set `{{x_vendor_token}}` in the environment.

**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `ReferralDashboardViewV1`  
**Module:** `Referral.views`  
**Route name:** `referral-dashboard-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

The referrer's own dashboard: their code, and this month's figures.

GET /api/v1/referral/dashboard/

SHARED PREFIX. Both surfaces show a referrer the same numbers about themselves, so it is universal by the surface rule and the class carries a bare `V1`.

IT MINTS A CODE ON FIRST VIEW, WHICH IS A WRITE ON A GET. Deliberate. RECHECKED 2026-10-07: narrowed from legacy's three writes to at most two inserts (`Referrer` via `get_or_create`, then `Referrer_Code`) inside one transaction - see `Referral.utils.issue` for why this one is kept and what the cleaner alternative would cost.

THE MONEY CONSTANTS COME FROM SETTINGS, NOT FROM THIS FILE. Legacy hardcoded 5000, 100000 and 20 in the view body, so changing a bonus meant a deploy and a code review of a view. They are settings with the legacy values as defaults, so nothing changes today and the next change is configuration.

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: wrapped as `{success, message, data}` by the
default `EnvelopeJSONRenderer`.
200 OK: `data` holds `referral_code`, `code_expires_at`,
`code_is_live`, `per_referral_bonus_amount`,
`monthly_target_amount`, `referrals_this_month`,
`referrals_eligible_this_month` (the `REFERRAL_MONTHLY_CAP` setting,
not a count), `total_successful_this_month`,
`total_awarded_this_month` and `referrals_needed_for_target`.
401 Unauthorized: missing or failed JWT, with
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`.
500: an internal error, detail in the span rather than the body.
```

request.description:
**Surface:** UNIVERSAL  
**View:** `ReferralValidateCodeViewV1`  
**Module:** `Referral.views`  
**Route name:** `referral-validate-code-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** POST  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Would this referral code be accepted for the caller?

POST /api/v1/referral/validate-code/

SHARED PREFIX, NOT `app-api/` OR `web-api/`. The rule is that writes stay shared and reads split by surface; this writes nothing and both surfaces ask the identical question about the same learner and read the identical answer, so it is universal and the class name carries a bare `V1`.

AUTHENTICATED, BECAUSE THE ANSWER DEPENDS ON THE CALLER. Two of the four refusals - self-referral, and a different code already applied - are facts about who is asking, not about the code. An anonymous version could only answer "does this string exist", which is the one question worth not answering: six characters from a 36-character alphabet is a small enough space to walk.

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: every answer is wrapped by the default
`EnvelopeJSONRenderer` as `{success, message, data}`; the shapes
below are what lands in `data`.
200 OK: `{"ok": true, "code": "<CODE>"}` - the code would be applied,
echoed upper-cased. The `"code": null` branch is UNREACHABLE: the
serializer refuses a blank or whitespace-only `code` with 400 before
`acheck` can return `None`.
400 Bad Request (refusal): `{"ok": false, "reason": "<outcome>"}` with
the display sentence lifted into the envelope's `message`. `reason`
is one of `invalid`, `expired`, `self_referral`,
`already_redeemed`.
400 Bad Request (body): `code` missing, blank, not six A-Z/0-9
characters, or an undeclared key - DRF's validation-error body.
401 Unauthorized: missing or failed JWT, with
`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`.
500: an internal error, with the detail in the span rather than the body.
```

`reason` AND `message` ARE DIFFERENT AUDIENCES. Legacy returned only a sentence, so a client that wanted to branch had to match on English prose. The outcome constants are part of the wire contract; the sentences are not.

Body template generated from `ReferralValidateCodeRequestSerializerV1`. Values are placeholders, not fixtures.

request.description:
**Surface:** APP  
**View:** `AppLikedAssetViewV1`  
**Module:** `Engagement.views`  
**Route name:** `app-favourites-v1`  
**Methods on this view:** GET  
**Authentication:** JWTAuthentication  
**Permission:** IsAuthenticated

Everything the calling learner has liked, grouped by what it is.

GET /app-api/v1/favourites/

THE CLASS SAYS "LIKED ASSET", THE PATH SAYS "FAVOURITES", AND THAT IS ON PURPOSE (maintainer, 2026-10-01). "Favourites" is the learner-facing word and is what legacy's route was called, so the path keeps it; the class is named for what it actually reads, which is `User_Like` rows. The naming standard wants path, route name and class to agree, so this is a recorded exception rather than drift - say the word and the path becomes `liked-assets/`, which costs nothing today because no client is bound to it yet.

APP-ONLY, hence the `app-api/` prefix and the `App` marker - reads split by surface, and there is no web twin today.

SCOPED TO `request.user` AND NOT ADDRESSABLE. There is no user id in the path or the query, so one caller cannot read another's favourites by guessing a UUID - the same reasoning as `ProfileViewV1`.

BOTH BUCKETS SHIP ON EVERY RESPONSE, empty as `[]` rather than omitted. A client that renders a section per key must not have a section appear and disappear depending on what the learner happens to have liked.

`reels` IS THE AI-IN-ACCOUNTING SECTION ONLY, not every CMS asset the learner has liked - see the note above this class for why, and for what that hides.

TWO QUERIES, NOT ONE PER ROW. Legacy issued one query and then walked `select_related` chains three relations deep per row to find the page a file belonged to. Both reads here are `.values()` projections that join what they need in SQL, so nothing is materialised and no lazily loaded relation is touched on the event loop.

Responses:

```
RECHECKED 2026-10-07: enveloped `{success, message, data}`.
200 OK: `data` is `{"masterclass": [...], "reels": [...]}`.
401: missing or failed Bearer token, from DRF before `get` runs.
500: an internal error, with the detail in the span rather than the body;
`message` is "Unable to load your favourites.", `data` is
`{"status": "error"}`.
```

The Programs screen's hiring-company wall, app surface.

`GET app-api/v1/programs/companies/`

THE LOGO WALL a learner sees under a program - the companies that hire from it.

REPLACES LEGACY `GET /companies/?page_key=program&category=CPA`, where the page and the category were query parameters on one shared endpoint. Here the surface is the route and the program is a declared parameter, so a mistyped category is a refusal rather than a different wall returned with a 200.

PAGINATED, and its web twin is a separate class over the same handler - two clients on different release cycles must not share an API class.

Authentication:

```
JWTAuthentication. JWT required.
```

Permission:

```
IsAuthenticated.
```

Method:

```
GET
```

Responses:

```
200 OK: The page of companies.
400 Bad Request: On a malformed query.
```

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `category` - Optional. Audience filter. One of: `CPA`, `CMA`, `CAIRA`, `USP`, `ALL`. Omitted, every active asset is returned. Sending both `category` and `show_to` with different values is a 400.
- `page` - Optional. Page number, 1-based. Omitted, the first page is returned.
- `page_key` - Optional. Which content tree to read. Matched case-insensitively against the asset's own section slug AND its root's slug. Example: `program`.
- `page_size` - Optional. Rows per page. Omitted, the paginator's own default is used (6 on the web contract); its `max_page_size` is the ceiling and it enforces both.
- `show_to` - Optional. The same audience filter under legacy's own name for this endpoint. Same vocabulary as `category`.

`GET app-api/v1/programs/webinars/`

The Programs screen's webinar rail, app surface. Replaces legacy `GET /program-webinars/?page_key=program&category=CPA`.

NOT PAGINATED, BY CONTRACT. At most one webinar comes back per programme - the next upcoming one - so there is no list to page. See `ProgramWebinarQueryV1`.

`page_key` IS NOT ACCEPTED. Legacy declared it and never read it: the scope is `Webinar.show_webinar_to_pages`, not a query parameter, and accepting a parameter that changes nothing is the shape `StrictInputSerializer` exists to refuse.

**Query parameters** - required ones are ticked, optional ones are pre-filled but unticked:
- `category` - Optional. Which programme's webinar copy to return. One of: `CPA`, `CMA`. NARROWER than the audience filter on the other rails.
- `page_key` - Optional. Which page scope to read from `Webinar.show_webinar_to_pages`. One of: `program`, `homepage`. Defaults to `program`.
